findings.topic: Rep ranges for fat loss / muscle retention
findings.summary: For a fat-loss goal where retaining muscle matters, moderate-rep resistance training (roughly 8-15 reps per set, 2-4 sets per exercise) combined with a modest calorie deficit is well supported for preserving lean mass better than cardio-only approaches. Total weekly volume per muscle group matters more than any single 'magic' rep number.
findings.source: ACSM Position Stand: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults (summary)

findings.summary: Beginners generally respond well to full-body sessions 2-4x/week, since each muscle group gets hit multiple times weekly, which accelerates early skill and strength gains compared to body-part splits.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (chapter summary)

findings.topic: Progression for untrained beginners with minimal equipment
findings.summary: Linear or double-progression (increase reps within a target range before increasing load/difficulty) works well for beginners and doesn't require heavy equipment — bodyweight and light-to-moderate dumbbell work is sufficient to drive meaningful early adaptation.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (chapter summary)
